If you are a massive horror fan looking for a game that actually keeps your heart pounding, Dead by Daylight is an absolute must-play. What makes this game so much better than other horror titles is that it doesn't just let you easily walk out the exit door. In too many games, escaping is entirely passive, meaning you either just run in a straight line until you win or you stop to solve a slow, boring puzzle. Dead by Daylight throws all of that out the window because as a survivor, you are constantly active. You have to repair generators under intense pressure, rescue your teammates from meat hooks, and nail stressful skill checks, all while listening for the terrifying heartbeat of an approaching monster. It turns every single match into a high-stakes, interactive slasher movie where your choices actually matter. On top of the fantastic survivor gameplay, the variety you get on the other side is unmatched because you have a massive roster of unique killers to choose from. Each killer comes with their own distinct powers, tracking tools, and playstyles. Whether you want to play a stealthy hunter, a chainsaw-wielding brute, or a supernatural monster, the game lets you step directly into the shoes of the ultimate horror villain. If you want a horror game that requires real strategy, team coordination, and delivers endless playability, stop waiting and go buy it!

Unfortunately, Dead by Daylight is coded with spaghetti. They have entire server rooms full of cooked noodles piled into metal boxes, and the entire company is so focused on trying to keep the pasta under control that I think sometimes the devs forget that the players also need to be having an enjoyable experience.

The good: you can play DBD for thousands upon thousands of hours and still not hit the skill ceiling. Both killer and survivor roles have a lot of nuance and can be genuinely fun to learn and to play. At it's best, it rewards the effort you put into it and can be a source of real connection with total strangers where everyone is having a good time.

The bad: It's harder and harder to find that best experience. Killers can wait in long queues to play against organized survivor teams that go out of their way to make it a horrible experience, with no ability to surrender a bad game and often not enough tools to punish survivor misplays. Some Killers are more accessible than others with built-in aim indicators, while others need an add-on and some have nothing at all. Many of the killers have buggy powers and will completely break into unplayability with random updates.

Survivors are punished with less points and/or boring games when killers using the most efficient tactics at their disposal (namely tunneling), leading to a frustrating and often toxic experience for both sides. Solo q still lacks meaningful communication tools, and teammates can sabotage you very easily both on purpose and accidentally. 

Both sides have extremely unbalanced perk combos, and many of the best perks in the game are paywalled behind premium characters. If you can't afford to buy the DLCs, you have to blindly wait for the perks to rotate through a weekly shop. The community is often toxic and an incredibly hostile environment for learning, while the game itself gives new players MINIMAL understanding of game mechanics. Either side can have games that are an endless pit of misery due to bad matchmaking, trolling, the truly endless supply of game-breaking bugs, or just RNG, and it's just...draining. I'm tired.

Eventually if you dare play anything that isn't meta this game will eat you alive, trying out a killer you haven't played with nothing to slow down the absurd speed of gens will end up with you getting queues longer than the games you play, playing with a good killer and or a good build will end up with the toxic community tbagging you or insulting you every chance they get, and if you dare try and play one of the 300 non meta survivor perks well a 5000 hour blight main on a streak will get you out of the game and you will have to watch your friends struggle for the rest of the match, the only saving grace is the few matches where you'll get players with the same goal as you, either you all tryhard and theres no one throwing your games, or you all have fun doing goofy stuff, but that's incredibly rare (which would be fixed by a ranked queue or even being able to toggle what kind of match you prefer in general by the way)

The new chapters are genuinely pretty good, appart from the perks that are always either unplayable or unfun for the other side, the characters themselves are often neat, but if they come from a license it's gonna cost you 5 bucks each (a tad less if you buy the whole chapter and not characters individually), and if they're not it's either 5 bucks each OR weeks of grinding, it's definitely better than it was a few years ago but that doesn't make any of this okay
the monetization in general is very bad, bhvr has poor quality control and likes to gut free rewards as time goes on, at least the paid pass pays for itself

For survivors the characters are just skins with perks attached, but for killer you'll see that every release is now bloated with your new flashy killer having a very complex power with multiple parts to overcompensate the fact that basic killers get nothing
the judgement, the killer we designed as a community, which just released at the time of writing, is pretty cool and very fun; you slingshot beams of light on survivors and can send them to a different realm where they fight for their lives, very cool
except you also get a buff that changes how your power works when you send a survivor to a realm
and you have altars around the map that act as special hooks for your realm which have specific properties and work very differently
and survivors you hit get debuffed so that they need to interact with altars (or wait a bit if they were in a realm) or they'll have harder skillchecks for everything
this killer shouldn't need 4 layers of bloat to make the fantasy work, it doesn't need bells and whistles to function, but since bhvr doesn't want to buff the killers as a whole you need to have gen regress and time wasters on top of perk counters baked into the power so that it doesn't get dumpstered on release, which then makes future killers even harder to make with powercreep
I can't even imagine trying to start the game for the first time and having to deal with that on top of learning the regular game, judgement isn't even that bad 

Bhvr also loves to ignore promises and generally sabotages themselves in very predictable ways, they have test servers for major patches and half of them for the past two years have been players begging the devs to not implement any of it because it's so fundamentally broken or misguided, like punishing killers for killing survivors too early (anti tunnelling) which also punishes you for literally doing your job well, in general bhvr loves to punish people instead of encouraging them to do something else, it's not "if you hook everyone instead of focusing 1 you get a buff" it's always "if you don't play as we say we'll make you unable to play the game", which unsurprisingly makes the game very frustrating 
They also have very poor management in general, for instance they rolled out the now called "pallet update" which added a good 10 pallets to half the maps in the game as a 1 line "quality of life" feature, as if the ressource management survivors need to learn isn't one of your most important macro skills
They're also very VERY slow to do basically anything asked of them, skull merchant was so problematic they announced a future rework by nerfing her into the ground so she's not a problem anymore (which is absolutely baffling on all fronts), and after a few blog posts about it and a whole year they announced that actually they gave up and buffed her up again, letting her be basically as is 

And lastly, the worst part by far, the gameplay
the fundamentals of the game are unfair and encourage you to play in the most unfun ways possible (tunnelling is optimal because it's 3v1 instead of 4v1, but 1 survivor has to not even play the game anymore, slugging is basically the same logic), instead of trying to fix any of that, encouraging killers to do anything else with basekit buffs or reworking the base game, they instead release band aid perks that "solve the problem" at the cost of having to run them every game "just in case"
over the years the survivors have been buffed basekit semi-regularely, with (until recently) 15 seconds of discretion and what is basically a layer of armor when they get unhooked, faster heals faster gens anti camp on hooks (most of them healthy changes for the game, albeit strong changes), whereas killers haven't gotten anything but nerfs for years
So what happens ? well since survivors are busted basekit killers have to switch to meta killers, meta perks or change games, and so since every killer is running busted killers with busted perks survivors also run busted perks and items to go with it, or else they end up on the ground for 5 minutes or out of the game in 3. 
The killer's genkick (which already takes up time with the animation and the fact you need to run to and then start to move out of the gen's area) loses the gen 5 seconds of progress and then 1/4th of a second of progress every second, meaning that one of their 4 survivor can just sit on the gen for 10 seconds and they'll undo what you spend 20 doing, the fact that this has remained unchanged for years, so much that one of the first tip i ever hear is "basically never kick", is just the perfect example of the balance team's priorities (aka buffing the role that has 80% of the players and agreeing to their every whim, fair or not)

In the end the only thing that this creates is one of the most toxic and entitled communities i've ever seen, on top of you being punished for wanting to branch out, play nice or generally wanting to be creative with your build and killers, on a game where the options for said builds is one of it's biggest appeals

I could go on and on about this game because in the end i love it, i want it to be better, and it's better now than it was on release or even 5 years ago, but it's such a slow, tedious process that it's just frustrating to watch, i don't regret playing it, but i wouldn't recommand it to most people unless it's what they always dreamt off
